terms.gloss: brittle: crisp, crunchy, breaking under the teeth
terms.comment: Pliny calls sugar dentibus fragile, brittle to the teeth; with dentibus the word says just what crunchy says. For the sound, crepāre (see the examples).

terms.gloss: toasted, roasted: crisp from the fire
terms.comment: The participle of torreō, for bread or nuts made crisp by heat.

phrases.latin: Crustula haec dentibus fragilia sunt; audī ut crepent!
phrases.english: These biscuits are crunchy; listen to them crunch!

phrases.latin: Pānem tostum mālō, quī sub dentibus crepat.
phrases.english: I prefer toast, the crunchy kind.

sources: Lewis & Short: fragilis · Lewis & Short: torreo · Lewis & Short: crepo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 73.
